leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part prize for B010 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, leaving out Knudsen, who is credited on the ballot, and Habener, who is not. Members cite the same scientific chain (proglucagon-derived peptides, the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) form, human incretin physiology, receptor biology, long-acting agonists, large outcome trials) and each says the opening unanimity is not itself the argument. They differ in citation wording: El-Manira's citation speaks of establishing the incretin axis, while the other five say the discoveries made incretin-based therapy possible. Not shared: the weight given to Knudsen's contribution and how firmly Mojsov's priority is held, since no member has verified it against primary records.

areas_of_agreement: All six members put B010 as the sole prize part with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as laureates, and none proposes a second part in the preferred configuration.

All six identify attribution, not the science or maturity, as the main weakness of B010: Mojsov versus the Habener group on priority for the bioactive peptide, Habener absent from the credited names, and Knudsen excluded by the three-person limit.
Four members (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) name B006 and B008 as alternatives; Perlmann and Sandberg name B006 and B020. All six name B006.

Several members (Svenningsson, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius) state that excluding Knudsen reflects the three-person cap and the discovery emphasis, not a view that her half-life-extension chemistry or industrial drug development was incidental, and that the citation should not suggest the drugs are an afterthought.

Members who commented on B006 (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) regard Rosenberg's claim as adoptive cell therapy broadly rather than CAR design. All six identify the absence of Eshhar from the credited names as a defect of any CAR-T configuration.
Members who commented on B008 agree that any three-person version (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) leaves Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck with credible claims and that the case is mainly methodological.
scientific_disputes: Whether the discovery-versus-tool distinction should weigh against B008: El-Manira holds that the Prize has rewarded methods that opened intractable questions, while Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius treat neuronal deployment as method development with limited clinical reach, and Perlmann drops it from his alternatives.

Whether B020 (unfolded protein response) belongs among the alternatives: Perlmann and Sandberg rank it third as a clean pair, while El-Manira and Svenningsson see its medical relevance as mostly conceptual or disease-associated so far. Perlmann also notes that PERK and ATF6, where others have claims, are outside the Walter-Mori core.

How much weight a prize citation should give the drugs themselves relative to the physiology. Svenningsson and Linnarsson would treat Knudsen as first reserve rather than displace a discoverer, while Sandberg says that naming the drugs would require reconsidering Knudsen at the cost of Mojsov or Drucker.

Whether B045 (SMN2 antisense) is mature enough: Svenningsson and El-Manira see a clear mechanism-to-drug arc but regard it as early and at risk of being read as recognition of antisense technology generally, and Sandberg calls it younger. Linnarsson ranked it third in the opening round, and B045 appears in no round-1 alternatives list.
attribution_disputes: B010: priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for identifying the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide is unresolved. Sandberg, Linnarsson, Svenningsson, El-Manira, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius all say they cannot verify it from the supplied record. Svenningsson and Sandberg would withdraw support if a documentary check showed Mojsov's contribution to be derivative.
B010: Habener is not among the credited names, so the committee cannot swap him in on this ballot. Linnarsson flags this gap explicitly.
B010: all six leave out Knudsen, who is credited on the ballot. The ballot lists four names and all six proposals take three, so the cut is a committee choice.

B006: five opening proposals named June, Sadelain and Rosenberg and Wahren-Herlenius named June and Sadelain. In round 1 El-Manira, Linnarsson, Sandberg and Svenningsson say they find the two-name version more defensible, while Perlmann would not reduce it before the Eshhar question is resolved. Eshhar is outside the credited names in every version.

B008: the six credited names are Boyden, Bamberg, Nagel, Miesenboeck, Deisseroth and Hegemann. All five opening proposals name Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann. Wahren-Herlenius asks why Deisseroth should be credited ahead of Boyden, and El-Manira, Svenningsson and Perlmann acknowledge that Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck have credible claims.

B020: Perlmann notes that Walter and Mori cover the Ire1 and HAC1/XBP1 core and not PERK or ATF6, where Ron and others have claims. Sandberg regards the Walter-Mori pairing as the cleanest on the list.

B044: Wahren-Herlenius says the exclusion of Sabatini should be argued on credit allocation and not on personal standing, and that attribution of mTOR protein identification among several groups is unresolved.
maturity_disputes: B010 is described by all members who address timing as mature and independently replicated, with long-term obesity outcomes and safety signals still accumulating. Perlmann asks how much weight those data should carry, and Svenningsson and El-Manira note that they do not affect the case for the discovery.

B006 has a clear clinical record but a fragile attribution, and Sandberg notes that it has no first-place support in the opening round. Whether that fragility is a maturity or an attribution issue is not settled.

B008 is judged by El-Manira and Svenningsson to have exceptional influence in neuroscience but only early clinical use, which Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius treat as a readiness problem for a Physiology or Medicine prize.
B020 has textbook maturity but, per Svenningsson, no established intervention yet. B045 is called early by Svenningsson, El-Manira and Sandberg.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann (stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, who is not on this committee. He reports no connection to any shortlisted candidate or credited name.
Svenningsson (chair) discloses co-authorship with Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. He reports no link to any shortlisted candidate.
Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and a shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation with colleagues. He reports no connection to any shortlisted candidate.
Linnarsson reports no specific conflict. He notes a recorded co-authorship with Sandberg and a KI affiliation, and no connection to any credited name.

Wahren-Herlenius reports past co-authors Vijay Kuchroo and Sven-Erik Sonesson and no involvement with any credited name. She notes that her field of autoimmunity and rheumatology is closest to B041 and B021, which she treats on the evidence like any other candidate.
Perlmann reports no specific conflict and no collaboration with any credited name.
No member reports a conflict requiring recusal on any shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: Can the documented record separate Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide from the Habener group's work well enough to defend her place? Which primary papers and dates would the committee accept as settling it?
If that check leaves Mojsov's priority unsettled, does the committee proceed with the three-name B010 allocation, or does it need a different name set that the supplied ballot cannot provide?

Should the B010 citation name the physiology and bioactive peptide only, or state explicitly that this work made the drugs possible? Is Knudsen the first reserve if any of the three names weakens, or does the cap settle her exclusion?

Does the committee prefer B010 as a stand-alone prize, or paired with a second distinct achievement (B006 or B008, with B020 for Perlmann and Sandberg)? If paired, how are three laureates split across two parts?

If B006 is the fallback, can it be given a defensible allocation when Eshhar is outside the credited names? Is June and Sadelain alone sufficient, or does Perlmann's condition that the Eshhar question be resolved first apply to any version?

If B008 is retained as an alternative, what documented basis ranks Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann ahead of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck? Does the committee treat optogenetics as a discovery or as a method for a Physiology or Medicine prize?
Which alternative should be the fallback if B010 does not secure four votes: B006, B008 or B020? Sandberg notes that this fallback is currently unclear.
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete convergence on a single B010 configuration, with six matching laureate sets, and the open questions concern documentation and wording rather than merit. Members agree that the main risk is the unverified Mojsov and Habener priority question and the Knudsen exclusion. Because no member has checked primary records, round 2 should treat that check as a precondition. Alternatives divide into B006 and B008 for four members and B006 and B020 for two, and the Eshhar gap is the only common attribution issue across B006 and B010.
